title: Bi-Lipschitz Coordinates at Regular Points of Noncollapsed RCD Spaces

issues.location: coordinates.tex, Lemma co:harmonic-normalization and the qualitative o(1) claims in pinching.tex (pi:qualitative-radial-error, pi:affine-improvement)
issues.description: Several uniform-in-center-and-scale statements are proved only by sketched compactness/contradiction arguments, for example the transformation induction across all dyadic scales and the uniform o(1) closeness of normalized columns at every center. Each looks standard (CJN/CN-style transformation theorem, which is valid because every ball near p is delta-flat at every scale), but the paper gives them only in outline. This is a matter of how fully the arguments are written out. I did not find an actual failure.
issues.evidence: The proof of co:harmonic-normalization runs the tau-normalizability improvement down residue classes mod m and identifies the mean Gram normalization by strong energy convergence (AH18). Its correctness depends on the uniform flatness (co:uniform-flatness) at all scales, and that flatness is correctly derived from Bishop-Gromov together with the bound density <= 1 at every point.

main_claim: Every n-regular point of a noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space has an open neighborhood that is L_n-bi-Lipschitz, in the restricted ambient distance, to an open subset of R^n, with L_n depending only on n.
sibling_notes: The family 357 board was empty when I started. The paper is self-contained and has no dependence on companion papers. Its key novel inputs are the summable directional pinching (Prop pi:directional-pinching) and the value-space iteration (Prop re:metric-iteration). Both survived my checks.
